title: Grateful Dead Live at Euphoria Ballroom on 1970-07-14
source: SBD > Master Reel > Dat> cd> shn> cd> ?> shn

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a rare 1970 acoustic/electric set, highlighted by How Long Blues, a jammed New Speedway, and an all‑time Cosmic Charlie despite a few tape cuts.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a clear, mostly pristine soundboard experience with occasional glitches and missing portions of Easy Wind and Good Lovin'. Musically the show shines – rare acoustic numbers like How Long Blues, a fiery New Speedway jam, and a thunderous Cosmic Charlie make it a must‑listen, while the electric set is solid though hampered by some cuts. Overall the performance and tape quality are strong enough to recommend this era‑defining concert.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the music and the tape, noting only minor glitches; weighted average of strong show (≈4.5) and good recording (≈4) yields a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp and clean overall with classic 1970 tape character; occasional glitches, tape‑machine slip on Easy Wind, and a noticeable cut in Good Lovin' but drummers sit high in the mix adding excitement.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed acoustic set with rare gems flows into a rocking electric half; transitions like China Cat → Jam → I Know You Rider are raw but exciting, though a few cuts interrupt the momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Classic tone and body on guitar; electric lead on New Speedway; notable solo on How Long Blues.
band_member_comments.Phil: Long, high‑in‑the‑mix solo in Good Lovin'; strong presence throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s cowboy‑tuned numbers pace the electric half; vocal slip‑ups noted but overall solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers are ‘smoking’, high in the mix, with funky percussion on China Cat → Jam and powerful drive on Good Lovin' and Cosmic Charlie.
